resources.string: A private messenger for two people.\nNo servers. No ads. No logs.
Messages are encrypted right on your device, before they are sent. The room password stays on your phone and is never sent to any server.
Atrum has no servers of its own. Messages travel over an open network already encrypted — anyone in between sees only scrambled data. No sign-up, no phone number.
Atrum is still evolving — some things may change or not be perfect yet. Just stay a little attentive. Thanks for trying it and helping make it better.

Perfect protection doesn\'t exist, and the author can\'t guarantee it. A lot depends on you: use strong invite passwords and share invite codes only through trusted channels. If a code leaks or ends up in an insecure messenger, your chat could in theory be read.
Photos and voice messages not sending?

In some countries, providers block part of the network. Try turning on a VPN or proxy — it doesn\'t affect your privacy: messages are still encrypted on your device before sending. This is a temporary measure while we work on more reliable delivery.
